To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
activated carbons from biomass and low rank coal are suitable for the preparation of cobalt-based catalyst for hydrogen production by the methanol decomposition.

the activated carbon texture is the main factor influencing the catalytic behavior of supported cobalt species in methanol decomposition, and the surface chemistry of the activated carbon matrix is a secondary factor, but it can be used to control the state and catalytical properties of supported cobalt.
activated carbons from waste and low rank coal can be successfully used as catalyst supports for the hydrogen production via methanol decomposition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of cobalt catalysts supported on activated carbon, and their use in methanol decomposition reaction.
the development of new and effective catalysts for methanol decomposition, which can be used for production of hydrogen in a fuel cell.
the development of novel catalysts for methanol decomposition based on the waste biomass and low grade coals as a source of carbon matrix and the cobalt as a catalytically active species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cobalt species deposited on the activated carbon surface with the highest specific surface area and developed mesoporous texture are the best catalyst for methanol decomposition.

the catalytic activity of cobalt species deposited on the surface of the activated carbon depends on the textural and chemical properties of the carbon matrix, and the most important factor is the specific surface area.
the most efficient catalysts are those with the highest cobalt content and the largest surface area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cobalt species are more dispersed and less reduced on the surface of the carbon matrix with higher surface area and micropore volume.
the most active catalysts for methanol decomposition are those in which cobalt species are in the form of Co2O3, Co3O4 and Co3O4/CoO mixtures.
activated carbons from waste and low rank coald can be used for preparation of active catalyst supports for methanol decomposition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalytic activity of cobalt species is significantly influenced by the surface characteristics of the carbon support.
the activated carbons prepared from waste biomass and coals can be used as a host for cobalt species in methanol decomposition reaction.
the cobalt species supported on activated carbon from waste biomass can be used as a potential catalyst for methanol decomposition to hydrogen.
